core_obligations: Part (1) (proof lines 13937-13945): R^n f_*F is the sheaf associated to V |-> H^n_etale(X x_Y V, F); taking V affine, the fibre product X x_Y V is quasi-compact and quasi-separated because f is, so the torsion statement applies and each section of the presheaf is a torsion group, whence the associated sheaf is torsion.

Part (2) (proof lines 13947-13955): the same computation with the unbounded description of the higher direct images of a complex, again for V affine, where X x_Y V is quasi-compact and quasi-separated; hence every H^n of the pushforward is torsion and Rf_*K is bounded below with torsion cohomology sheaves.
proof_roadmap: Describe the higher direct images of a sheaf and of a complex as the sheafification of the presheaf V |-> H^n(X x_Y V, -).
Restrict to affine V so that the fibre product is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
Apply the torsion statement to conclude in both the sheaf and the complex case.
difficulty_reason: The lemma records that torsion is preserved by higher direct images along a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism, for a single torsion sheaf and for a bounded below complex with torsion cohomology sheaves (statement lines 13923-13934). The proof (proof lines 13936-13955) uses the presheaf description of the higher direct images on affine V, where the fibre product is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and invokes the torsion statement for that case. H2: one uniform computation applied twice, written out.
